problem: Given a curve $x=5{y}^{3}-8{y}^{2}+16,$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(24,2)?$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2y-\frac{6}{y}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2y-6{y}^{-1}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)-6\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1}) \\  & =2(1)-6(-{y}^{-2}) \\  & =2+6{y}^{-2} \\  & =2+\frac{6}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2{y}^{2}+6}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{2{y}^{2}+6}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(4,3)} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{2}}{2(3)^{2}+6} \\  & =\frac{9}{24} \\  & =\frac{3}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-3 & =\frac{3}{8}\cdot (x-4) \\ y & =\frac{3}{8}x-\frac{3}{2}+3 \\ y & =\frac{3}{8}x+\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
